items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: When he was with Basie. ... Here in Los Angeles, when they came out here. And this was a say around '37.

ctx.x: Do you remember the Grey Brothers' first names?

I can't think of them right now. And, at the same time, Walter Page, who was Count Basie's left hand, had a band of his own, in Oklahoma City. And he was playing Benny Moten bass saxophone. So, now, April 1st is when Billy Morton died from a tonsillectomy. They severed an artery, and he hemorrhaged to death. And, meanwhile, I was hoboeing out here. I got to Amarillo and got the word.

Walter Page gave up his band. The band's name was the Blue Devils. And Count Basie organized a band that was broadcasting from the Reno Club. And he had mostly members of Benny Moten Billy Morton's band. So he -- Walter Page joined Count Basie
